After breakfast, your driver will take you to the airport for the flight to Cusco. On arrival, you’ll be met and taken to your hotel. After a short rest, set out on an afternoon sightseeing tour by bus.

Cusco lies at over 3,000 metres above sea level. According to local tradition, the city was founded by Manco Cápac, who came here from Lake Titicaca. The first stop is Sacsayhuamán, a 15th-century fortress and temple complex. Its walls are built from enormous blocks in the Cyclopean masonry style. The largest stones weigh more than 3,000 tonnes and were brought from far away.

Next you’ll see Q’enqo, a rock-cut complex associated with Inca religious ceremonies, as well as Puka Pukara and Tambomachay, with its network of water channels.

You may feel the altitude within your first few hours in Cusco, so there’s time to rest before the tour. The scale changes throughout the afternoon, from the massive walls of Sacsayhuamán to Q’enqo’s narrow passages, and from Tambomachay’s water channels to the stone foundations of Qorikancha. Together, these sites show how Inca heritage survives across the city and the surrounding area.

Next is Qorikancha, the Golden Temple and the principal shrine of the Inca Empire. The temple was destroyed after the Spanish arrived, and its foundations were used to build Santo Domingo. According to tradition, Qorikancha’s walls were covered with gold, and inside stood a golden altar and a large disc depicting Inti, the sun god.

**Cusco Cathedral**

Optional visit

Allow about 40 minutes. The visit costs $25.

After the tour, return to the hotel.

Lima: historic buildings with dark balconies, palm trees and flower beds
Cusco to Machu Picchu and back

After breakfast, meet your English-speaking guide and transfer to the railway station. The train takes you to the Aguas Calientes area, the starting point for the trip to Machu Picchu.

The Inca city existed for just over 100 years. It is associated with the ruler Pachacuti, under whom a residence and sanctuary was built here with palace rooms, houses for the nobility and temples. Machu Picchu lies at around 2,450 metres among steep mountain slopes. The stone buildings follow the contours of the land, and the blocks fit together with remarkable precision.

The city’s remote location helped it escape destruction by the conquistadors. It became widely known in 1911 through the American explorer Hiram Bingham. Machu Picchu has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983 and one of the New Wonders of the World since 2007.

In the afternoon, descend to Aguas Calientes and have lunch at a restaurant serving Peruvian cuisine. Then take the train back to Cusco, where you’ll be met at the station and taken to your hotel.
